 Joe Root has had his lbw issues in the past and Sri Lanka would be wise to use that ball against him.

 Nothing from the umpire, but Sri Lanka decide to review with what looks like a punt.

 Dunith Wellalage's over starts with three dot balls, ends with three singles.

 Harry Brook takes a single off Dunith Wellalage, getting the ball past a cover fielder.

 Eng 96-2 published at 17 overs 17 overs 
 Joe Root gets his boundary count going, whipping Dasun Shanaka through mid-wicket and then sending a second shot a little closer to mid-on.
 New batter Harry Brook spends the entire over at the non-striker's end.
 35 5 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 10:16 BST 10:16 BST 
 Alex Hartley 
Former England bowler on Test Match Special 
 Ben Duckett was so fluent a couple of days ago. He has struggled on this surface. They knew it was going to be tougher batting first with the bounce. A sticky innings for Duckett but that was hitting the middle of middle stump.
 13 34 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 WICKET published at 16 overs 16 overs 
 Duckett lbw b Wellalage 29 (Eng 85-2) 
 Image source, Getty Images And England's figures against left-arm spin get even worse!
 Dunith Wellalage bags his second England opener, trapping Ben Duckett lbw as the batter misses a sweep.
 Duckett consults with Joe Root but decides not to appeal - that did look pretty out with impact right in front.
 A challenging day for Duckett, with his 29 runs coming from 39 balls. He was starved of the strike initially, but did pick things up a little towards the end of his innings.
 16 98 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 How's stat?! published at 10:13 BST 10:13 BST 
 Image source, CricViz In ODIs since the start of 2025, England are one of the worst performing sides against left-arm spin in terms of average (27.35). Of the 12 full member nations, only Australia and West Indies have a lower average against that particular type of bowling in the time frame.

 Eng 78-1 published at 15 overs 15 overs 
 Dasun Shanaka into the attack.
 Ben Duckett takes a two in the covers off the seamer's opening delivery, with no further runs coming off the rest of the over.

 Eng 76-1 published at 14 overs 14 overs 
 Joe Root comes out to the middle and immediately takes a single down the ground.
 Two runs and one wicket off Dunith Wellalage's third over - he's enjoying himself after surprisingly being left out of the team on Tuesday.
 19 7 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 10:06 BST 10:06 BST 
 Alex Hartley 
Former England bowler on Test Match Special 
 He's just picked out that fielder perfectly at long off. If you had to pick where to put a fielder it would be there. He didn't have to move an inch. Another diasppointing end to a Tom Banton fifty. He was striking the ball well and unfortunately for him, he's given his wicket away.

 WICKET published at 13.2 overs 13.2 overs 
 Banton c Liyanage b Wellalage 50 (Eng 74-1) 
 Image source, Getty Images Tom Banton's handy innings comes to an end.
 He shuffles towards leg and tries to lift Dunith Wellalage over extra cover, but picks out Janith Liyanage. 
 Banton looks disappointed - he was well set there.

 Post published at 10:02 BST 10:02 BST 
 Steven Finn 
Former England fast bowler on BBC Test Match Special 
 It's the first time Duckett's timed one properly today and I think he just waited a little bit more. Back-to-back boundaries and both nicely timed.
 32 3 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Eng 74-0 published at 13 overs 13 overs 
 14 runs from Eshan Malinga's over and they're all Ben Duckett's!
 He hits a trio of twos and then finishes the over by hitting his first two fours, hitting through extra cover and mid-wicket.
 He moves from nine to 23.
 32 2 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 How's stat?! published at 10:02 BST 10:02 BST 
 Image source, CricViz 50* (49) for Tom Banton, who has found all but one of his boundaries through the offside through crisp stroke-play and innovative shotmaking against spinners. It's his fourth fifty in the format, and has moved his ODI average to just a shade under fifty (48.80).
 23 2 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 More delays in South Africa-Australia Test published at 10:02 BST 10:02 BST 
 Image source, Getty Images More rain in Gqeberha. The Australian rain dance is working. 
 There should have been 75 minutes of play on the final day of the second Test by now. 
 Australia couldn't get away with this, could they?
